title: Moonshot AI 在 HuggingFace 开放 2.8T 参数 Kimi K3.1 Pro 权重
content:
Rohan Paul· @rohanpaul_ai · X·· 29 分钟前精选AI 评分76
AI 导读
Moonshot AI（@Kimi_Moonshot）在 HuggingFace 开放 Kimi K3.1 Pro 权重（https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro）。
推荐理由
原文汇总了 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的权重开放、架构细节、基准成绩与许可证条款，读者可据此评估其部署成本与实际能力边界。
正文 · AI 翻译
Moonshot AI 在 Huggingface 上发布了 2.8T 参数的大规模 Kimi K3.1 Pro 权重。
在 Terminal-Bench 上，它与 Claude 5.5 正面交锋
以 4-bit 权重训练，也以该精度发布，避免了 16-bit 副本所需的 5.6TB。
Moonshot 将稳步上升的漏洞利用技能追溯到其通用中期训练语料和 RL 环境中埋藏的网络安全内容，并在开放权重前将两者移除。
在 Moonshot 自己的测试中，该模型在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上得分 65.7%，接近 Claude Opus 5.5 的 66.4%，但在无工具情况下在 HLE-Diamond 上仅达 39.4%，而 GPT-6 Astra 为 65.8%。
每个 token 仅激活其 104B 参数，其 93 层中有 69 层使用线性注意力，这使得处理 1M token 上下文更便宜。
其修改版 MIT 许可证豁免内部使用，但要求年收入超过 2000 万美元的模型托管公司进行谈判，以约束可能压低公司自家 API 价格的转售商。
来源：Rohan Paul · x.com

report.summary: Moonshot AI released 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights on HuggingFace, trained and shipped in 4-bit, with a modified MIT license targeting large resellers.
report.background: Open-weight releases have shifted from 7B hobby models to frontier-scale mixture-of-experts systems, and Chinese labs — Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu — have used them to win developer mindshare against closed US APIs. Kimi's K-series established Moonshot as a long-context specialist; K3.1 Pro pushes that to 2.8T total parameters with only 104B active per token, a sparsity ratio that keeps inference affordable while scaling knowledge capacity. Two industry undercurrents shape this release. First, 4-bit-native training and distribution is becoming practical: shipping a 16-bit copy of a 2.8T model would mean a 5.6TB download, which almost no one can host. Second, open-weight licenses are growing teeth — Meta's Llama license and DeepSeek's model license both impose conditions, and Moonshot now adds a revenue threshold aimed squarely at commercial resellers rather than researchers, a template likely to spread as labs try to protect API margins while keeping community goodwill.
key_points: Scale vs. cost: the model holds 2.8T total parameters but activates only 104B per token, so compute per generated token stays in the same class as much smaller models. That sparsity, plus 4-bit native weights, is what makes a trillion-scale open release downloadable and servable at all rather than purely a benchmark artifact.

Architecture favors long context: of 93 layers, 69 use linear attention instead of full quadratic attention, which cuts the cost of handling 1M-token contexts. This continues Moonshot's long-context positioning and matters for codebase-scale or document-scale agent workloads where context length, not raw IQ, is the bottleneck.

Benchmarks are split: 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 is essentially parity with Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4%, but 39.4% on HLE-Diamond without tools trails GPT-6 Astra's 65.8% badly. Reading: strong at agentic terminal/coding loops, weaker at closed-book hard reasoning — a profile consistent with heavy tool-use training.

4-bit-native release: training at 4-bit and publishing at that precision avoids a 5.6TB 16-bit distribution, roughly a 1.4TB download instead. This is a real precedent for how frontier open weights get shipped, though it also bakes in quantization choices downstream users cannot easily undo.

Safety scrubbing and a bespoke license: Moonshot traced rising exploit-writing skill to cybersecurity content in mid-training corpora and RL environments and removed both before release. The modified MIT license exempts internal use but forces model-hosting companies above $20M revenue to negotiate, targeting resellers who would undercut Kimi's own API pricing.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a signal that frontier-scale open weights are now a deliberate competitive strategy, not a loss-leader. A 2.8T model at near-parity with a top closed model on agentic coding compresses the pricing power of closed APIs and forces every lab to justify its margin with something other than raw capability. For developers, the practical win is optionality: a self-hostable model competitive on terminal and coding agents, with cheap 1M context, reduces lock-in — but the 1.4TB download, cluster requirements, and baked-in 4-bit precision mean only well-funded teams can actually serve it. Smaller teams will consume it through hosted providers, which is exactly what the license targets. For regular users, expect cheaper long-context and coding-agent features across products within months, since hosted derivatives are the fastest route to market. The safety scrubbing is also notable: labs are now editing training data to remove capability, not just adding refusals.
report.tools: Start at the HuggingFace repo (moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) for config, tokenizer, and license text before planning any deployment. For serving, watch vLLM and SGLang for MoE plus linear-attention kernel support — hybrid attention stacks usually need upstream work — and KTransformers or llama.cpp-adjacent projects for CPU/GPU offload of 4-bit expert weights. Monitor Terminal-Bench 4.0 and HLE-Diamond leaderboards to sanity-check the claimed parity yourself, and track the license's $20M clause if you plan to resell inference.
